newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico parties reassured, cautioned by envoy-paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico parties reassured, cautioned by envoy-paper.

text.p: Foreign investors would not necessarily flee Mexico if an opposition party were to win congressional elections next month, the U.S. ambassador to Mexico was quoted as saying Wednesday.
But if the winning party did anything to make them feel unwelcome, investors might sell immediately, the U.S. envoy, James Jones, added.

"Investors would abandon Mexico in a minute if the winner -- of any political party -- did things which sent signals in the sense that private investment was not welcome in Mexico," Jones told the newspaper Reforma.
But, he added, "I don't expect any of the leaders of the major political parties to take that posture."
A press spokesman was not available at the U.S. embassy to confirm the report.
Jones, who is leaving his post at the end of the month, has previously said the United States does not mind which of Mexico's three main political parties wins the July 6 elections.
But he told the newsweekly Proceso in an interview: "If the winner of the elections does anything silly, investors will leave Mexico in a flash."
